- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +2% above prior peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature mean reversion.
- Model frequently underestimates true price in early forecast horizon (e.g., day 1–5) when sentiment is neutral or negative; adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% for first 3 days.
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive, model lags in reaction; forecast should rise 1–2 days ahead of sentiment change.
- If model forecast is >10% above true outcome for 3+ consecutive days, apply downward correction of 1–2% per day until convergence.
- For sentiment history with alternating highs/lows, model tends to overfit recent sentiment; use 2–3 day moving average of sentiment to smooth forecast bias.
